rationale:
Checked `REGRESSIONS.md` first: the heatmap and volcano_r drops at v1 were caused by an unrelated sandbox Write-hook stall (max_turns, no answer.md) in runs where the skill hadn't even loaded, not by anything v1 added to the skill body — both recovered to their noskill pass rate by v2, so there was nothing in the current (v2-derived) body to reverse.

Across box/composition/dotplot/heatmap/volcano_r the wiki consistently shows the skill loading inconsistently (0/3-2/3) but never changing the outcome, since the model already solves these standard scanpy/pandas patterns correctly unaided — per the instructions, a load-rate gap with no outcome effect is lower-value than a body gap that changes outcomes, so I left the description untouched rather than risk overfitting it further.

The one task with a real, outcome-changing, body-fixable gap is `volcano`: across noskill/v1/v2 the pseudobulk+PyDESeq2 pipeline is fully specified by the task prompt (exact threshold, design, contrast, alpha), yet agents still land on slightly different significant-gene counts (835/838/839) because each hand-rolls the pseudobulk aggregation and the covariate dtypes differently, with no check to catch a silent row-count/total mismatch or an accidentally-numeric grouping covariate. I added two generalizable fixes to the body (not tied to this dataset): (1) a new default check that a grouped aggregation (pseudobulk, groupby-sum) must produce exactly one row per group and conserve each column's total, since two equivalent-looking implementations (groupby vs. one-hot-matmul) can silently drop/duplicate rows; (2) sharpened the existing "set factor levels explicitly" rule to call out that a blocking/grouping covariate (batch, replicate, donor) in a model formula must be cast to character/factor, since a numeric ID silently fits as a continuous slope instead of one coefficient per level with no error. Both match the skill's existing "silent data loss" check philosophy and should reduce run-to-run variance on any aggregate-then-model pipeline, not just this one.
